name: NIST Artificial Intelligence page: standards, testing and manufacturing AI
title: NIST Artificial Intelligence page: standards, testing and manufacturing AI
answer: This is NIST's Artificial Intelligence overview page. It describes NIST's AI work in research and development, testing and evaluation, guidelines and standards, and best practices. Its most useful point for manufacturing readers is that NIST integrates AI tools, guidelines and frameworks into measurement science and measurement services, and works through the Center for AI Standards and Innovation and an AI Economic Security Center for U.S. Manufacturing Productivity. The page also says NIST produces voluntary guidelines, tools and resources for trustworthy and responsible AI.

sections.body: NIST publishes this page. It is a broad web overview, not a detailed technical report or standard. Its scope covers NIST's AI research and development, testing and evaluation, guidelines and standards, best practices, and partnerships. It names work through laboratory programs, the Center for AI Standards and Innovation, and manufacturing and critical infrastructure centers. The text states no publication date. The page was harvested on 2026-09-26.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: NIST says its AI efforts focus on research and development, testing and evaluation, guidelines and standards, and best practices. It argues that better understanding of how AI technologies function helps companies trust, adopt and export American AI. NIST is investing in research to improve consistency in measuring AI system performance, reliability and security, spanning scientific machine learning models to language models and agentic AI. NIST is building an AI testing and evaluation ecosystem, aiming to keep the U.S. government at the forefront of evaluating frontier models and promoting American AI innovation. NIST produces voluntary guidelines, tools and resources for trustworthy and responsible AI. It works through laboratory programs, the Center for AI Standards and Innovation, and partnerships including the AI Economic Security Center for U.S. Manufacturing Productivity and the AI Economic Security Center to Secure U.S. Critical Infrastructure from Cyberthreats. NIST researchers use AI to conduct experiments autonomously, generate datasets and glean information from historical data. Integrating AI tools, guidelines and frameworks into measurement science and services is described as critical for AI adoption in domain specific environments, especially critical and emerging technologies and manufacturing. NIST efforts include developing standardized, often first of their kind methods, data, models and tools, and enabling their incorporation into development workflows, manufacturing and production. The stated goal is to help industry experts make faster, more reliable predictions of biological, chemical and materials properties, for example through autonomous research and development laboratories.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no specific numbers, dates or quantitative benchmarks. It states that NIST produces voluntary guidelines, tools and resources for trustworthy and responsible AI. It states that NIST is building an AI testing and evaluation ecosystem and aims to keep the U.S. government at the forefront of evaluating frontier models. It names the Center for AI Standards and Innovation, the AI Economic Security Center for U.S. Manufacturing Productivity, and the AI Economic Security Center to Secure U.S. Critical Infrastructure from Cyberthreats. It also states that integrating AI into measurement science is critical for adoption in critical and emerging technologies and manufacturing, and that autonomous research and development laboratories can generate high quality data.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in manufacturing would use this page as a high level map of NIST's standards, measurement and testing work. It shows where manufacturing appears in NIST's AI program, including the AI Economic Security Center for U.S. Manufacturing Productivity and the statement that AI integration into measurement science is critical for manufacturing adoption. It also points to voluntary guidelines and testing and evaluation as the vocabulary and tools NIST offers. It is useful for orientation, not for detailed implementation guidance.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Manufacturing

sections.body: This is a broad overview page, not a standard, technical report or case study. It does not give detailed requirements, timelines, funding figures, adoption metrics or specific manufacturing use cases. It states no publication date in the text. It is a government source, not commercial, but it is partial and high level, so readers should treat it as a starting point and follow the named programs for substance.
